h: Tips for a Bluewater Day That Actually Works
p: Combining a shopping trip and a trampoline session takes a bit of planning, so here's how to make it painless. Book your Gravity slot first and plan your shopping around it, rather than the other way round. If the kids are bouncing first, you'll have a calmer crew for the shops afterwards. If they're bouncing last, it's a great carrot to dangle while you browse.

Fill in waivers online before you arrive, and pack water, comfy clothes and a spare top for the drive home. Grip socks can usually be reused, so keep them somewhere safe for your next visit. Make a note of where you've parked, as it's easy to get turned around in a big shopping centre car park.

Bluewater sits right on the edge of the Kent Thames-side area, so there's plenty nearby once you've had your fill of the shops. Gravesend is a short drive east, with its riverside promenade, the town pier and a statue of Pocahontas in the churchyard of St George's Church, where she was buried in 1617.

Ebbsfleet International station is close by, with fast trains into London, so you could easily make a weekend of it. If you want some fresh air, the Darent Valley to the south-west has gentle walks and pretty villages, while Dartford Heath is a big, open space just down the road.
